name: Cory Booker

issue_poll.name: Rutgers-Eagleton/SSRS Garden State Panel poll, Dec 29, 2025-Jan 6, 2026, 1,570 NJ adults (open-ended top priority), combined with Pew Research Center national survey, Sept 28-Oct 4, 2026 (share of registered voters calling each issue very important)
issue_poll.note: No fall 2026 New Jersey poll with a published issue ranking was found (Rutgers-Eagleton's April and October 2026 releases covered affordability only; no Senate-race issue poll found). Base order from the Rutgers-Eagleton NJ poll: taxes 28% (mostly property taxes), affordability/cost of living 19%, utility costs 9%, housing 7%, economy 5% (merged with cost of living), health care 4%, education 3%, government issues incl. corruption 3%, opposing Trump agenda 2% (dropped: not a testable issue), immigration 2%. That poll asked about priorities for the governor, so national 2026 polling was used to complete and order the list: Pew (https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2026/10/08/economy-ranks-as-top-issue-in-midterms-for-all-voters-but-partisans-differ-over-the-importance-of-other-issues/) economy 84%, future of democracy 73%, health care 68%, education 62%, immigration 59%, foreign policy 57%, energy policy 54% (merged with utility costs), violent crime 52%, abortion 46%. Democracy/government ethics placed above education (tied at 3% in Rutgers; Pew 73% vs 62%). Ranks 9-10 (foreign policy, crime) added from Pew as the highest-ranked issues missing from the NJ list.

issues.detail: Keep Your Pay Act: first $75,000 of joint income federal-tax-free; child tax credit $3,600 ($4,320 under 6) plus $2,400 baby bonus; expand EITC.
Oppose and challenge Trump tariffs in the Senate; secure federal funding for Gateway and Delaware River Bridge projects; act against corporate consolidation.
Pass Power for the People Act (S.3682): data centers, not household ratepayers, pay grid and transmission upgrade costs they cause.
Expand affordable housing using the recent federal housing law and opportunity zones (existing law); no new target.
Lower health care costs and expand coverage; oppose ACA and Medicaid cuts.
18-year term limits for Supreme Court justices; bar justices from accepting gifts from parties with interests before the Court; binding ethics rules for justices.
Vote against DHS budgets adding ICE funding until ICE accountability and hiring standards are imposed; keep state/local role separate from federal enforcement.
Vote against funding to continue the Iran war; assert Senate war powers to end it; support two-state solution and more Gaza humanitarian aid.

plan_caveats: No fall 2026 NJ issue-ranking poll found; base NJ poll is from Dec 2025-Jan 2026 and asked about priorities for the new governor (all adults, not likely voters). Pew national (Sept-Oct 2026) used to complete and order the list.
Taxes rank 1 in NJ largely because of property taxes, a state/local matter; the Keep Your Pay Act (federal income tax) is Booker's campaign answer. No 2026 position found on the SALT deduction.
Energy rated Concrete on a bill Booker co-introduced in Jan 2026 (campaign year); no campaign material found that touts it, so it is closer to in-office record than a campaign pledge. Judgment call.
Keep Your Pay Act is also a Senate proposal (Mar 2026), but campaign coverage (WHYY, Fox 29) names it as his central 2026 campaign plan.

Democracy/ethics positions come from a Meet the Press interview (June 21, 2026) as reported by Breitbart; no campaign-site text was readable (corybooker.com could not be fetched; Ballotpedia shows no 2026 survey).
Immigration rated Partial: the vote pledge is conditional on undefined 'accountability' standards. Source is a Jan 2026 interview on a budget fight.
Health care rated Vague: no 2026 commitment found to extend ACA credits or reverse Medicaid cuts in his own words; only criticism and general goals.
Education and crime rated None after searching; his Camden police visit (June 2026) produced no stated position.
Booker campaigned largely on opposition to Trump and the Iran war; Oct 8 Rider University debate coverage reported few domestic specifics.
